title: qianshou/capability/v1
description: The node's capability DECLARATION (section 2 of the contract, the foundation). A node states a semantic capability plus the concrete implementation binding that satisfies it — never a bare package name. See contracts/README.md §2.2 and decision one. FIELD PROVENANCE: provides/impl/health/limits and the impl={runtime,version,path} shape come from the phase brief's node example verbatim; `native_binaries` is NOT from the brief — it is the platform's real field name (core/worker.py:63, storage/repo.py:1892, engine/planner.py:925, services/workers/heartbeat.py:78,109) and is included so this contract can pin the field that was misspelled `native_bins` for two months. `contract` const added by this draft. DELIBERATELY OPEN ROOT: `additionalProperties` is absent on the root object so a newer node can add keys without breaking a v1 reader. Key discipline for the root is therefore NOT enforced here — it is enforced by the three-stage unknown-field funnel (README §3 决定二), which is why the mutation test targets this document. Nested `impl` and `limits` stay closed where they are contract-owned shapes.

provides.description: Every capability this node claims, each with the concrete implementation that backs the claim. A claim without an impl binding is not a claim — that is the whole point of decision one. The same semantic capability may be satisfied by different implementations on different nodes (three OCR packages, two whisper variants); see capabilities.registry.json.

capability.description: Semantic capability name from capabilities.registry.json, e.g. `media.transcode`. MUST be a registry member: an unregistered name is an unfulfillable promise, and the contract test rejects it.

impl.description: The concrete binding. `runtime` MUST equal an implementation id registered for this capability, so a node cannot claim media.transcode while binding to an unrelated tool.

runtime.description: Implementation id, e.g. `ffmpeg`, `pytesseract`, `faster_whisper`. This is the layer that is allowed to change without touching the task that asked for the capability.

version.description: Version of the implementation as the node measured it (e.g. ffmpeg `8.0.1`). Free-form string because vendor version schemes are not uniform; min_version matching is therefore a code-level comparison, not a schema constraint.

path.description: Absolute path of the executable, for binary runtimes. Absent for library/in-process runtimes (e.g. a python package). NEVER trust this path for execution without re-verifying it on the executing node.

prompt_style.description: Prompt style the local model or generator accepted, copied from the node's own probe. Absent when the model did not report one. Never invented from a package name.

loras.description: Installed LoRA metadata the local model reported. Absent when the probe did not receive any.

trigger.description: Trigger word the installed LoRA actually uses. Copied from the probe; never guessed from the model filename.

health.description: Result of the node's own probe at declaration time. `missing` lets a node keep a capability listed (and its binding visible for diagnosis) while stating it cannot currently serve it. A scheduler must not treat a non-ok capability as a match.

limits.description: Upper bounds the node is willing to accept for this capability. Deliberately a free-form object for now, but every key present must be one the platform understands; a limit the platform ignores is worse than no limit, because the task believes it is bounded.

max_input_mb.description: Largest single input this node accepts, MiB. Positivity is NOT machine-enforced (numeric bounds are outside the enforced subset).

max_concurrency.description: Concurrent shards this node will accept for this capability.

native_binaries.description: EXACT NAME: `native_binaries`, plural, full word. This is the platform's own field (core/worker.py:63). It was sent by clients as `native_bins` for two months; storage/repo.py:1811-1814 dropped the misspelled block silently, with no error and no log, while registration still reported success. This contract exists partly to make that naming collision impossible to reintroduce — see the mutation test in contracts/tests/contract.spec.ts.
